notes: Retain every failed/interim log and native capture. Initial TypeScript/SDK/lint issues were resolved before final gates; an early UI mock returned undefined for an async Remove and was fixed to resolve normally.

The first owned OLE filesystem fixture returned E_INVALIDARG. Shell namespace APIs require display DOS/UNC names rather than verbatim Rust I/O paths; construct an IShellItemArray before binding BHID_DataObject. Final real IDataObject and real IFileOperation owned tests pass.

The first native script called an island-only Shelf command from the tray. It now uses the allocated island and reacquires pages after native compact lifecycle teardown. The c native attempt ran the earlier executable while the next build was pending, so is explicitly nonauthoritative.

Native hover initially lacked its native drag lease and the surface closed. OLE enter/leave/drop now set/cancel the lease, with generation protection against late cancelled enters; the StrictMode regression and owned native copy/Undo flow cover it.

Early DownloadDone native fixtures used SQLite datetime text without the RFC3339 timezone expected by the production row parser, so metadata failed before the action appeared. Correct the fixture timestamp and assert actual metadata/suggestions before rendering. Review actions also route into expanded Files and survive result expiry, covered by StrictMode and a native wait beyond the TTL. The warm native view establishes behavior, not cold-start performance.

Default axe found pin accessible names excluding visible metadata, unnamed generic action groups, missing file-drop heading and hovered verb contrast4.16. Use natural names/descriptions, semantic groups, a real heading and existing foreground token; no rule exclusion. Pin popup is audited as the captured component because the separate underlying expanded frame is visually overlapped; other scenes audit the whole document.

Early capture setup used a parent without direct font glyphs and an incomplete metadata IPC allowlist; final audit selects rendered text and allows only the new read/plan/watch lifecycle calls. No execute/copy/Shell/clipboard commands are allowed in visual captures. Duplicate transient outgoing DOM is avoided by scoping the hovered target to the live drop content.

Move/tool drafts clear on collapse to prevent replay; DownloadDone review and Ctrl/Shift pin drops remain explicit. Header close keeps the reference pin peek360x274 with four footer actions rather than wrapping an extra footer button.

One native Peek repeat failed after the first capture helper settled only briefly. That first failure retained hashes/log but no pair buffers; the improved helper saves both failed PNGs and DOM diagnostics, and final native captures settle naturally for1200ms before the repeat check. No content/time/CSS freeze. All retained M10 PNGs decode under the stricter300000-byte limit, independently of the historical harness300KiB bound. Natural browser motion/caret/device metrics and exact repeated bytes remain; no edited pixels, product-state freeze, secret waiver or unreviewed accessibility result.

The first staged whitespace check found Windows PE-manifest resource padding. Keep exact raw manifest bytes in deterministic gzip and commit normalized XML text. The updated independent resource audit repeats against the same executable and pins raw/canonical hashes; no whitespace waiver.

Initial staged/directory Gitleaks scans flagged the already-referenced Figma document identifier under the generic field name fileKey. Store the same document as its design URL instead; retain redacted finding reports and original scan logs, with no detector waiver or ignore-file change. Later scans are authoritative.
